questions.q: Which Snowflake object should Power BI connect to, and why?
options: VW_DAILY_TICKET_SUMMARY, because it already has the right grain and scope baked in, so Power BI doesn't need to duplicate that logic in DAX
RAW_TICKETS, because Power BI always needs the most granular data available
SUPPORT_WH, because that's the warehouse name
DRIFTWOOD_ANALYTICS, because the database name alone is enough to connect
questions.explain: Connecting to the view means every visual in the report builds on logic that's already correct and tested, instead of re-deriving GROUP BY logic in DAX.

questions.q: Which Snowflake role should Power BI use to sign in?
options: DRIFTWOOD_SUPPORT_ANALYST — the same read-only role built and granted SELECT in Lessons 6 and 7
An admin role, since it's more convenient and avoids permission errors
No role is needed since views don't require RBAC
A new role created specifically and only for Power BI's internal use
questions.explain: Power BI should connect with the least-privilege role already set up for this exact purpose, not an admin account.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Import mode and DirectQuery in Power BI?
options: Import copies the query's current result into Power BI's own model (a snapshot until refreshed); DirectQuery sends a live query to Snowflake on every interaction
Import is always slower than DirectQuery
DirectQuery only works with raw tables, never with views
Import requires a paid Power BI Premium license; DirectQuery does not
questions.explain: Import trades always-current freshness for speed and simplicity by snapshotting the result; DirectQuery stays live but costs more per interaction.

questions.q: Why is Import mode the right choice for this specific report, rather than DirectQuery?
options: The data volume is tiny and a refresh before a weekly meeting is current enough — this isn't a minute-by-minute dashboard with heavy concurrent use
DirectQuery is not supported for Snowflake at all
Import mode is required whenever RBAC is involved
The VP of Support specifically requires DirectQuery for compliance reasons
questions.explain: DirectQuery earns its cost when true real-time freshness or very large data is required — neither applies to a small weekly ticket summary.

questions.q: What three pieces of connection information does Power BI need to reach this view, and where do they come from?
options: The Snowflake account identifier, the warehouse (SUPPORT_WH), and the database/schema (DRIFTWOOD_ANALYTICS.SUPPORT) — all already decided in the Lesson 2 plan
A brand-new database, a brand-new warehouse, and a brand-new schema created specifically for Power BI
Only a username and password — no other configuration is needed
The exact row count of RAW_TICKETS, entered manually
questions.explain: Nothing new needs to be invented at connection time — the account, warehouse, database, and schema were all named back in the Lesson 2 plan.
